title: AWS Cloud API Error Rate Spike

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with permission to search `index=aws`.
• Install and configure: Splunk cloud TA for AWS.
• Ensure `aws:cloudtrail` events are flowing (prerequisite UC: 4.4.33 when applicable).
• Map `aws` and field extractions per `docs/guides/aws.md`, `docs/guides/azure.md`, or `docs/guides/gcp.md` as appropriate.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=aws sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail.
Expected sourcetype: `aws:cloudtrail`. Validate with:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail"
| table _time action user resource
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
The search scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` and applies `*` to surface `AWS Cloud API Error Rate Spike`. Tune time range and alert threshold to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare result counts to the vendor console (CloudTrail Event history, Azure Activity Log, GCP Logs Explorer, or service-native UI). Spot-check `_time` and actor fields. Confirm CIM acceleration only after TA field mappings are verified.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_53_alert` with appropriate severity. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) empty results — verify TA input and index routing; (2) duplicate events — check S3/SQS duplication; (3) missing fields — upgrade `Splunk cloud TA for AWS` and review `props.conf` aliases; (4) alert fatigue — add CMDB/allow-list exclusions documented in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for aws cloud api error rate spike in your cloud audit logs so the team catches important changes early instead of finding out from auditors or customers.
